principles.text: Don't chase a sector-wide gap up (IGV +6% in a day, OKTA/CRWD gapping above resistance) - wait for the pullback into the rising 9 EMA instead of buying strength; a gap up that pulls back into the rising 9 is the long entry.

On a gap-up day the shorts are the weak names gapping INTO resistance: the declining 9/21, the gap-down anchored VWAP, the 50 EMA, or a cluster of long upper wicks (APLD, RDDT, COIN, BE, AAOI examples).

A volume spike on a wide expansion candle after a prolonged uptrend (PATH riding the 9 EMA for a month) is treated like a parabolic tell: sell some into strength, because pauses usually come with a burst of volume and volatility. Keep the rest if it's only day one of a tiny-flag breakout.
Short the weakest name in a weak group (QBTS vs RGTI/IONQ): if the group rolls over, the weakest gets the strongest follow-through.

Avoid shorting a huge wide-range intraday candle after earnings/news when the daily trend is still up (HPQ rejecting the 21 EMA with the 9 above the 21 and the 50 rising); the better trade there is a pullback long into the 50 EMA. Flagged as a topic to study.

It is never wrong to sell some into strength and book profits; selling is an art with no perfect rule. A useful tell: when you feel hyped or want to share your happiness about a position, sell some to keep mental calm.
Take many tiny tries on a short (SPCX: two losses of ~0.1-0.15% each, then a third try) until the name genuinely clears resistance or closes above the weekly 9.
Self-critique: a pullback into the 21 EMA that stops slightly ABOVE the prior swing high is too aggressive an entry - wait for it to go a little lower.
Gold/silver shorts: don't be early - wait for the close below the 9 EMA first.

After an enormous run (1000%+ in about a year) a weekly failed breakout with downside follow-through is the dot-com leader topping pattern: most huge-run leaders top after the failed breakout that follows the first pullback and bounce.
Turn off other traders' streams when they start influencing how you feel about the market; trading alone for a period can be a good thing, and learning to deal with loneliness is part of the job.

Opening range breakouts worked on the software theme today, but the base success rate is too low; find the criteria/environments that make ORBs work by studying it yourself - the answer you dig out is your edge.
Adopting price alerts when there are too many names to monitor in a day.
Only NVDA going higher while the other large caps do nothing 'feels odd'; strength today was software and crypto, weakness was semis (weak names rejecting resistance).
AMD: failed reclaim of the 50 and 21 EMA and a push lower to the 9 - a short candidate tomorrow if it stays weak.
Watching streams or reading books doesn't make anyone profitable: understand your own edge and fix your own mistakes; thank yourself, not the streamer.
